project.name: Sprint 14 — Merge Verification
project.description: Five different devs branched off the same base this sprint, each fixing something different. Standup this morning: "everything's merged into main, ready for release." Before you sign off, you need to actually verify it - not by asking around, but by walking the graph and checking, for each fix, whether it's actually reachable from main right now.

start.speaker: Narrator
start.narrative: You pull up the graph. Five devs, five branches, one claim that all of it made it into main. You decide to check each fix one at a time instead of taking the standup update at face value.

c1.message: chore: branch off for sprint 14 fixes

c2.message: fix: null check crash on checkout

c3.message: fix: race condition in save queue

c4.message: fix: memory leak in asset loader

c5.message: merge: combine checkout fix and asset-loader fix

c6.message: fix: validation edge case on empty cart

c7.message: fix: timeout bug in payment retry

c8.message: merge: cherry-pick timeout fix into release/hotfix

c9.message: merge: combine sprint 14 fixes into main

check-priya.speaker: You
check-priya.narrative: Dev 1 of 5: Priya. Her checkout fix feeds into the merge that combines checkout and asset-loader, which feeds directly into main's tip.
check-priya.prompt: Is Priya's fix live on main right now?

choices.label: Yes - it's an ancestor of main's tip
No - can't be sure without walking it again

priya-flag-note.speaker: Narrator
priya-flag-note.narrative: You walk it again anyway. It holds up - Priya's commit is main's ancestor, two hops back through the merges.

check-sam.speaker: You
check-sam.narrative: Dev 2 of 5: Sam. His save-queue fix branches off the same base commit - but nothing else points back to it. It's sitting on its own, unreachable from any of the merges.
check-sam.prompt: Is Sam's fix live on main right now?

choices.label: No - it's never referenced by any merge

sam-pushback.speaker: Priya
sam-pushback.narrative: "That's odd," Priya says, "I thought the save-queue race condition was still open - I'm not seeing Sam's fix anywhere in staging."

sam-escalate.speaker: You
sam-escalate.narrative: You've got a direct signal that contradicts what you just told the team, and you called Sam's fix live without actually tracing it back from main.
sam-escalate.prompt: Do you double-check the graph, or stick with what you said?

choices.label: Stick with it - reassure the team

sam-recover.speaker: You
sam-recover.narrative: You trace it properly this time. Sam's commit isn't an ancestor of main's tip through any path - it's just sitting there, branched off and never merged. You correct yourself.

sam-worse.speaker: Narrator
sam-worse.narrative: You reassure the team Sam's fix is live and Priya must be seeing something stale. It isn't stale, and she wasn't wrong.

sam-bad-ending.speaker: Narrator
sam-bad-ending.narrative: The save-queue race condition - the bug Sam's fix was actually meant to close - ships untouched. It resurfaces in production two days later, corrupting saves during peak traffic.

ending.debrief: Priya gave you a direct, correct signal, and you overruled it with an answer that was never traced against the graph in the first place. Sam's commit was never an ancestor of main - it was just sitting on its own branch. Version Control exists precisely so "whose fix is live" doesn't depend on who argues more confidently in the room.

check-devon.speaker: You
check-devon.narrative: Dev 3 of 5: Devon. His asset-loader fix isn't a direct parent of main's tip - it feeds into an earlier merge first, which then feeds into main.
check-devon.prompt: Is Devon's fix live on main right now?

choices.label: Yes - it's still an ancestor, just not a direct parent
No - it's not main's direct parent, so it can't have made it

devon-pushback.speaker: Devon
devon-pushback.narrative: "Wait, are you sure? I watched my branch get merged myself, and that merge is definitely somewhere upstream of main."

devon-escalate.speaker: You
devon-escalate.narrative: "Not a direct parent" and "not an ancestor at all" aren't the same claim, and you just treated them as if they were.
devon-escalate.prompt: Do you trace the full ancestry, or defend your answer?

choices.label: Trace the full ancestry, not just the direct parent
Defend it - if it's not the direct parent, it's not in

devon-recover.speaker: You
devon-recover.narrative: You trace the full chain this time, not just one hop. Devon's fix feeds into the checkout/asset-loader merge, which feeds directly into main. It's live - two hops back, but live.

devon-worse.speaker: Narrator
devon-worse.narrative: You insist Devon's fix isn't in, since it's not main's direct parent. Devon, trusting your read, spends the afternoon re-diagnosing and re-patching a memory leak that was already fixed - and the duplicate patch conflicts with his own already-merged one.

devon-bad-ending.speaker: Narrator
devon-bad-ending.narrative: Untangling the conflict between Devon's original fix and his own duplicate re-fix costs more review time than the original bug would have.

ending.debrief: "Not the direct parent of the tip" and "not an ancestor" got treated as the same thing, and they aren't - a merge commit's ancestry runs through every one of its parents, not just the most recent one. Devon's fix was two hops back but genuinely live, and treating it as missing sent him to redo work that was already done, then conflict with it.

check-aisha.speaker: You
check-aisha.narrative: Dev 4 of 5: Aisha. Her cart-validation fix is a direct parent of main's tip commit.
check-aisha.prompt: Is Aisha's fix live on main right now?

choices.label: Yes - it's a direct parent of main's tip
No - can't be sure without walking it again

aisha-flag-note.speaker: Narrator
aisha-flag-note.narrative: You walk it again anyway. It holds up - Aisha's commit is a direct parent of main's tip.

check-marcus.speaker: You
check-marcus.narrative: Dev 5 of 5: Marcus. His payment-timeout fix was merged - but into "release/hotfix," a completely separate ref. Nothing on main points back to it.
check-marcus.prompt: Is Marcus's fix live on main right now?

choices.label: No - it's merged into a different branch, not main
Yes - it's merged, that's what matters

marcus-pushback.speaker: Riley
marcus-pushback.narrative: "Hang on," Riley asks, "merged into what, though? We're releasing main today, not release/hotfix."

marcus-escalate.speaker: You
marcus-escalate.narrative: That's a fair question, and "it's merged somewhere" was never the same claim as "it's merged into main."
marcus-escalate.prompt: Do you go back and check which ref Marcus's fix actually landed on, or defend it as live?

choices.label: Check which ref it actually landed on
Defend it - it's merged, that's good enough

marcus-recover.speaker: You
marcus-recover.narrative: You check properly - Marcus's fix landed on release/hotfix, a completely separate ref from main. It's real, it's merged, and it is not on main.

marcus-worse.speaker: Narrator
marcus-worse.narrative: You defend Marcus's fix as live. The team skips testing the payment-retry timeout path in today's release, since it's marked as already fixed.

marcus-bad-ending.speaker: Narrator
marcus-bad-ending.narrative: The payment-retry timeout bug ships in the main release - because it only ever existed on an unrelated hotfix branch, not on main.

ending.debrief: "It's merged" and "it's merged into main" are different claims, and the gap between them shipped a known bug straight into a release. Marcus's fix genuinely exists, signed and merged - just onto release/hotfix, a ref nobody was releasing today. Version Control means checking which ref a commit actually reaches, not just whether a merge happened somewhere.

resolution-clean.speaker: Narrator
resolution-clean.narrative: Five fixes checked: three live on main (Priya, Devon, Aisha), two not (Sam still unmerged, Marcus only on release/hotfix). You report exactly that before sign-off, not the flattering version from standup.

good-ending.speaker: Narrator
good-ending.narrative: Release notes go out accurate. Sam's and Marcus's fixes get scheduled for the actual release that will carry them.

ending.debrief: Five fixes, two different reasons two of them weren't actually live: one branch never merged at all, one merged onto the wrong ref entirely. Neither would have shown up from trusting the standup update - only from actually tracing each fix's ancestry against main's real tip. That's what Version Control is for: the graph settles "is it live," not who says so most confidently.

resolution-recovered.speaker: Narrator
resolution-recovered.narrative: You get to the right answer on all five in the end. But it took Riley's question to catch that Marcus's fix was only ever on release/hotfix, not main.

neutral-ending.speaker: Narrator
neutral-ending.narrative: The release notes go out accurate in the end, corrected just before sign-off.

ending.debrief: You got there - but only because someone else asked which ref Marcus's fix actually landed on. "It's merged" is a claim that sounds complete and isn't; the whole point of Version Control is having the actual ref checked before anyone has to ask the follow-up question.
